video_title: Dillon Brooks BREAKS DOWN The LeBron Meme, 3,000 Makes A Week & His NEW Villain Role

quotes.speaker: Dillon Brooks
quotes.summary_phrase: Dillon Brooks on his evolution into a leadership role
quotes.excerpt: the villain role changed over time when I started taking on a lot more leadership role.
quotes.quote: The villain role changed over time when I started taking on a lot more leadership role. When I got to Phoenix, that was my thing, to try to instill confidence. When I got to Phoenix, that was my thing.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye on Dillon Brooks' impact as a culture bringer
quotes.excerpt: my boys who live in Phoenix appreciate the fact that they didn't know you are culture bringer.

text_blocks.speaker: Channing Frye
text_blocks.text: One, being a Phoenician—Richard, throw the hat down, Richard—being a Phoenician, we are Phoenicians. We appreciate the shit out of you. Two, my boys who live in Phoenix, fuck with you heavy. And I think my boys who live in Phoenix appreciate the fact that they didn't know that you are a culture bringer. That is invaluable in the NBA.

quotes.speaker: Dillon Brooks
quotes.summary_phrase: Dillon Brooks on his transition from Memphis to Phoenix
quotes.excerpt: I feel like I left stuff on the table in Memphis with my all-around game.
quotes.quote: I think it was a dream come true. It is kind of a second coming to me. I feel like I left stuff on the table in Memphis with my all-around game, and now, once I got traded, I felt like the opportunity was there again to seize it. Phoenix has been great, I love the coaches, I love my players, and the fans are exquisite.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on Dillon Brooks' career evolution as a player
quotes.excerpt: watching you start off as a defender and you built your reputation to Memphis.

text_blocks.speaker: Richard Jefferson
text_blocks.text: I covered you at Oregon, and watching you start off as a defender and you built your reputation to Memphis. Memphis was still trying to replace you as the 3-and-D offensive player. Go to Houston, you start the culture in Houston. Obviously, Kevin Durant, look, he is Kevin Durant, right? It is like, you know, Giannis, these guys pop up, shit happens. But you go to Phoenix and you are a part of that shifting culture and you have your best numbers of your career.

text_blocks.speaker: Dillon Brooks
text_blocks.text: I am addicted to it, addicted to just seeing the ball going in the net. I haven't felt this way at the beginning of my career. I got lost in the sauce of the NBA to start my career, and then once the last two years, like you said with Houston and then got to Phoenix, that is when it started really picking up.

quotes.speaker: Dillon Brooks
quotes.summary_phrase: Dillon Brooks on learning from Kobe Bryant and Michael Jordan
quotes.excerpt: how they prepare themselves each summer how to get better with pledging yourself to the work.
quotes.quote: I am taking things from the greats, like Kobe Bryant and Michael Jordan and those guys, how they prepare themselves each summer how to get better with pledging yourself to the work and then doing it every single day, no excuses.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on Dillon Brooks' role as an agitator
quotes.excerpt: you have to willingly play not necessarily the villain role. First of all, you sit courtside.

text_blocks.speaker: Richard Jefferson
text_blocks.text: You have to willingly play not necessarily the villain role. First of all, you sit courtside watching that shit. You are a villain.

text_blocks.speaker: Richard Jefferson
text_blocks.text: No, but it is more I look at it more as an agitator, right? You need agitators on your team if you want to compete at a high level.

quotes.speaker: Allie Clifton
quotes.summary_phrase: Allie Clifton on Jordan Ott's praise for Dillon Brooks
quotes.excerpt: where would we be without Dillon Brooks? I don't think any of us want to think about it.

text_blocks.speaker: Allie Clifton
text_blocks.text: Your head coach, we asked him before the game started about your impact and Jordan Ott said, 'Where would we be without Dillon Brooks? I don't think any of us want to think about it.' His competitive fire, his grit, what he brings every single night, whether he feels 100% or not, is something unique in the NBA.

text_blocks.speaker: Dillon Brooks
text_blocks.text: I would say because the villain first came out with me just like cussing guys out, talking shit, doing like controversial like hits, elbows, pushes, fights, whatever. But I feel like I evolved it more by just being diligent with my work and then doing it every single day, no excuses.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on the potential of LeBron James and Dillon Brooks
quotes.excerpt: the same way that Kobe and Matt Barnes used to have their beef and then Kobe recruited.

text_blocks.speaker: Richard Jefferson
text_blocks.text: The same way that Kobe Bryant and Matt Barnes used to have their beef and then Kobe recruited Matt Barnes. Me and him are crazy. LeBron James fucks with us because we are crazy. If there was ever a time, and I will guarantee you this, I don't know what that competitive dynamic, but could you see him and LeBron playing together?

text_blocks.speaker: Dillon Brooks
text_blocks.text: I watch him all the time.

text_blocks.speaker: Richard Jefferson
text_blocks.text: I am not talking about the talking shit. I mean the same way that Matt Barnes would throw like act like he was going to hit Kobe with a ball and then two years later, Kobe is talking to his kids because he respects Matt Barnes. LeBron plays to be the greatest player ever. He needs people that are psycho enough to challenge him.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye on Dillon Brooks' trash talking
quotes.excerpt: I say something to LeBron one time, I say, 'Yeah, I am going to get traded.'

text_blocks.speaker: Channing Frye
text_blocks.text: I say something to LeBron one time, I say, 'Yeah, I am going to get traded.' But I said, 'Man, fuck that dude.' Right? But then I was like, 'Ooh, ooh.' And then you got traded.

text_blocks.speaker: Dillon Brooks
text_blocks.text: I didn't get traded till three years later, but you know, listen, your brother was getting old and they had to play Kevin Durant to play fire.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on respecting players you talk trash to
quotes.excerpt: people don't understand how much you can talk shit to a player, but also respect them.

text_blocks.speaker: Richard Jefferson
text_blocks.text: People don't understand how much you can talk shit to a player, but also respect them. You are not looking for his respect, he is not looking for your respect, but at the end of the day, you know it is there and the game talks. I have been around enough players to be like, 'Hey, LeBron, what do you think about us getting Dillon Brooks?' She is like, 'Yeah, bring that motherfucker. If he going to talk shit to me, he will talk shit to fucking anybody.'

text_blocks.speaker: Dillon Brooks
text_blocks.text: Those are the people that you want on your side.
